site.name: Fenn Type Office
site.statement: Typefaces, and the things _they’re set in._
site.lede: **Ilse Fenn and Joaquim Ruo**, a two-person studio drawing type and designing what it is used for: identities, posters, books and signs. Since 2014.

projects.title: Gannet Sans
projects.outcome: A grotesk in 9 weights, licensed by 140 studios in year one

image.alt: A specimen poster: a huge condensed Gg over four lines of Gannet Sans from thin to heavy.

case.intro: A condensed grotesk drawn for headlines that have to fit, in 9 weights from Thin to Heavy.
body: Gannet started as the lettering for a festival poster and grew into a family when three clients asked for the poster type by name. The narrow widths keep their counters open at small sizes, so the same family sets a 40-metre banner and a 9-point caption.
The specimen poster is printed in one black on uncoated stock; the waterfall runs through four of the nine weights.

projects.title: Haverland season 25/26
projects.outcome: 38 concerts, one numeral system across every poster

image.alt: A season poster: the numbers 25 in red and 26 in blue overprinting on cream paper.

case.intro: One numeral system for a whole season: every poster is built from the date, overprinted in two inks.
body: The orchestra plays 38 concerts between September and June. Each poster sets the concert’s date as two overprinted numerals, so the season reads as one family on a wall of other posters.

projects.title: Kestrel Rail wayfinding
projects.outcome: One sign family for 31 stations, drawn to read at 40 m

image.alt: A green platform sign reading Perron 4, Platform 4, on a white tiled station wall.

case.intro: A sign family for 31 stations, set in a version of Gannet Sans opened up to read at 40 metres.
body: We tested every sign at full size on the platforms before fabrication. The arrow, the pictograms and the type were drawn together, so a sign with no text still has the same rhythm as one with two languages.

projects.title: Field Notes covers
projects.outcome: Twelve covers built on a single five-bar grid

image.alt: Three book covers fanned on a table, green, cream and red, each with five bars.

case.intro: A series of twelve essays, each cover built from the same five bars set to the length of its chapters.
